page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n4.xlarge is a shared-core virtual server instance positioned in the entry-level compute segment. Powered by an Intel Xeon Skylake 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this KVM-based virtual machine provisions 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. The processor architecture includes support for AVX and AVX-512 extensions, alongside AES and BMI2 bit-manipulation instruction sets. Memory is provisioned at 8.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB allocated per vCPU. The instance does not include dedicated hardware accelerators, featuring zero GPUs, and provides no bundled local NVMe or SSD storage, requiring attached network storage. Baseline networking throughput is capped at 1 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

Benchmark measurements indicate entry-level performance characteristics consistent with shared CPU resource models. In multi-core CPU evaluations, the server produced a Geekbench multi-core score of 2301.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 5186.07, placing overall processing capability in the lower 25th percentile. Single-core execution reflects similar bounds, with Geekbench single-core registering 847.0 and stress-ng recording 1106.08. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 31.31 GB/sec, while large-block write operations achieved 27.61 GB/sec, representing middle-tier throughput for memory writing. Data processing tasks demonstrated restricted throughput, with single-threaded gzip compression at 18.8 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 13.64 GB/sec.

The shared CPU allocation model delivers cost-effective resource density for applications that tolerate variable or capped processor performance. Because CPU cycles are shared across physical hardware, execution latency and raw compute power exhibit tradeoffs compared to dedicated compute tiers. The instance achieves 4.54 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 3.3 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. These performance dynamics align with lightweight non-critical workloads, development and testing environments, low-traffic web applications, staging nodes, and low-volume utility services that do not require continuous compute saturation or bundled local disk IOPS.

Built on the x86_64 architecture using an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz, it provides two physical cores with hyperthreading over a KVM hypervisor. Hardware features include AVX-512 and AES instructions, with no integrated GPUs and no bundled local storage, operating alongside a 1 Gbps baseline network capability. Synthetic benchmarks establish lower-quartile performance metrics across Geekbench, PassMark, and compression utilities, while memory write bandwidth remains moderate at 27.61 GB/sec. Given its shared-core configuration and modest throughput profiles in web serving and Redis testing, this server functions as an economical resource for background utility tasks, staging environments, testing pipelines, and non-critical low-traffic web hosting.
